title: A dual expression plasmid with Microcin B17 compatible with both prokaryotic and mammalian systems
author: Murakami, Nagatomo, et al.
materials: Cell culture and lipofection were performed using standard protocols [7]. HEK293 cells (ATCC CRL 1573; ATCC, Manassas, VA, USA) were cultured in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum. Exponentially growing cells were plated onto 35 mm dishes, and transfection was carried out using commercially prepared lipofectamine (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA).

steps.title: Amplify MccB17 gene by PCR
steps.instruction: Use high‑fidelity Pfu DNA polymerase (Agilent) with the primers listed in Supplementary Table 1 to amplify the MccB17 toxin gene (without leader peptide). Run 25 PCR cycles: 98 °C denaturation for 10 s, annealing at the calculated temperature (~50 °C) for 30 s, and extension at 72 °C for 30 s.

steps.title: Digest PCR product and vector
steps.instruction: Digest both the purified PCR product and the pgMAX‑II plasmid with EcoRV and XbaI at 37 °C for 45 min, then separate the fragments on a 1.5 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Purify DNA fragment from gel
steps.instruction: Excise the correct band from the agarose gel and purify the DNA using a gel‑extraction kit with a standard ion‑exchange column (Macherey‑Nagel) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Ligate insert into pgMAX‑II vector
steps.instruction: Ligate the purified insert into the EcoRV‑XbaI sites of pgMAX‑II using Takara DNA ligase and incubate the ligation mixture at 16 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Transform ligation into Turbo‑competent E. coli
steps.instruction: Mix 0.1 mL Turbo‑competent E. coli (New England Biolabs; K12 genotype: F’ proA+B+ lacIq ΔlacZM15 / fhuA2 Δ(lac‑proAB) glnV galK16 galE15 R(zgb‑210::Tn10)TetS endA1 thi‑1 Δ(hsdS‑mcrB)5) with the ligation product, incubate on ice at 4 °C for 25 min, add 0.9 mL LB medium, and recover by shaking at 200 rpm for 1 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells on selective agar
steps.instruction: Spread the recovered culture onto LB agar plates supplemented with ampicillin and incubate at 37 °C for 16 h.

steps.title: Isolate plasmid from a single colony
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony, inoculate into 4 mL LB broth containing ampicillin (150 µg/mL), shake at 200 rpm for 12 h at 37 °C, harvest cells by centrifugation at 6800 × g for 1 min, and purify plasmid DNA using the FastGene Plasmid Mini Kit (Nippon Genetics Europe).

steps.title: Culture HEK293 cells
steps.instruction: Grow HEK293 cells (ATCC CRL 1573) in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum; plate exponentially growing cells onto 35 mm dishes.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293 cells with plasmid
steps.instruction: Transfect the plated HEK293 cells with the purified pgMAX‑II/DsRed/MccB17 plasmid using Lipofectamine (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Incubate and assess fluorescence
steps.instruction: Incubate transfected cells for 48 h, then examine DsRed expression under a fluorescence microscope (excitation 563 nm, emission 582 nm) and record the red fluorescence.

description: •Materials and methods•Plasmid construction•The pgMAX-II plasmid, which contains the lac promoter and lac operator, was used for plasmid construction (Fig. 1A) [6,7]. As previously reported, pgMAX-II contained a CMV promoter and a poly-A sequence, facilitating direct expression analysis in both prokaryotic (E. coli) and mammalian cells without additional DNA recombination [7]. MccB17 polypeptide was prepared by PCR-based amplification using oligo DNA primers [8] (Supplementary Table 1).Fig. 1A. Diagram of the pgMAX-II/(His)/MccB17 dual expression system. The pgMAX-II plasmid system contains two promoters: a CMV promoter for mammalian expression and a lac promoter (Lac P.) and operator (Lac O.) for prokaryotic expression. The MccB17 toxin sequence was inserted between EcoRV and XbaI. The target gene (green arrow) is inserted at the EcoRV site, resulting in a chimeric fusion protein that includes a poly-histidine tag sequence (His: in green) and toxin gene (blue arrow). The mammalian expression unit, comprising the CMV promoter and poly-A tail, is also shown (in red). (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)Fig 1•Methods•DNA recombination was performed according to a modified standard method [9]. In brief, PCR was performed to construct the plasmid. The amino acid sequences of CcdB and MccB17 are presented in Fig. 1A [8]. MccB17 peptide toxin gene without leader peptide sequence was inserted between the EcoRV and XbaI restriction sites. The conditions for PCR using high-fidelity Pfu DNA polymerase (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA) were empirically modified (25 cycles of denaturation at 98 °C for 10 s, annealing at the calculated temperature [∼50 °C] for 30 s, and extension at 72 °C for 30 s).
